mechanism_narrative: Persistent negative WORKPLACES mobility (-12.9% at t-0w) signals continued remote work adoption. This suppresses commuter-adjacent retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks as workplace-anchored shopping patterns remain disrupted.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has remained between -12.6% and -13.4% for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES rises above -10% in any week of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (+7.0% at t-0w, sustained above +6% for four weeks) indicates households remain home-anchored. This behavioral lock-in suppresses discretionary retail-and-recreation visits as consumers prioritize essential shopping (GROCERY_PHARM) over leisure retail, producing lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +6% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has been consistently elevated at +6.1% to +7.0% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases week-on-week in three or more of the next four weeks, or RESIDENTIAL falls below +5% while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined sharply and consistently (from -26.1% to -32.4%), indicating outdoor recreation is suppressed. This signals either weather deterioration or behavioral avoidance. Suppressed outdoor leisure predicts continued suppression of retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two weeks as the underlying constraint persists.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -30% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -26.1% at t-3w to -32.4% at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -25% in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC increases despite PARKS remaining below -30%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has stabilized near -18% to -19% across four weeks, indicating consistent public-transport suppression (likely policy-driven capacity limits or behavioral avoidance). Persistent transit friction prevents retail-district access, constraining RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains between -18% and -20% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has remained in the range -18.4% to -19.6% across all four weeks
regime_hint: transit capacity restrictions or pandemic-driven avoidance
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -15% in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC increases despite TRANSIT remaining below -18%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained stable and only moderately negative (-11.6% to -13.9%), while RETAIL_REC is substantially more negative (-18.6% to -21.3%). This divergence indicates consumers are prioritizing essential shopping over discretionary retail. If this preference persists, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed relative to essential categories over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above RETAIL_REC by more than 5 percentage points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC is 6-8 percentage points lower than GROCERY_PHARM across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC gap to GROCERY_PHARM narrows to less than 3 percentage points, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility are both suppressed and correlated (both near -18% to -19% at t-0w). This joint suppression indicates a coordinated reduction in commuting activity. If commuting remains suppressed, the ecosystem of retail-adjacent to transit and workplace corridors will remain depressed, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fall below -18% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both near -18% to -19% at t-0w
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT rises above -15% in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC increases despite both remaining below -18%.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a slight uptick from t-1w (-21.3%) to t-0w (-19.3%), a 2-percentage-point improvement. If this marginal recovery trend continues at the same rate, RETAIL_REC will improve further over the next four weeks, producing a positive direction relative to the last 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC improves by at least 1.5 percentage points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -21.3% at t-1w to -19.3% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in two or more of the next four weeks, or the week-on-week improvement rate falls below 0.5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation (+7.0%) combined with PARKS suppression (-32.4%) indicates households are confined indoors. This indoor confinement regime suppresses all out-of-home mobility including retail. Only if PARKS mobility recovers (signaling outdoor access restoration) will RETAIL_REC recover over the next four weeks. Absent PARKS recovery, RETAIL_REC remains depressed.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above +6% AND PARKS below -30% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is +7.0% and PARKS is -32.4% at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above -25% in any week of the forecast period and RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points, or RESIDENTIAL falls below +5% while RETAIL_REC increases.
